title: Warm orange and rhubarb compote with yoghurt

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Fruit, honey, cinnamon, almonds, pumpkin seeds and natural yoghurt are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Forced rhubarb, oranges, almonds, pumpkin seeds and natural yoghurt are all stocked by Tesco in January at everyday prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a grater, a saucepan, a frying pan and a bowl, and peeling oranges with a knife is within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: 400g rhubarb, three oranges and 500g yoghurt make a fair breakfast for four, and a short covered simmer with honey and juice suits tender forced rhubarb.

honest_times.reason: Zesting, peeling and slicing three oranges, cutting the rhubarb and toasting the nuts while it simmers fits believably into 15 minutes hands-on and 20 in total.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient is used, nothing unlisted appears in the steps, and 'Forced rhubarb' is the same food as the rhubarb id.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm compote of early forced rhubarb and winter oranges suits a cold January morning, and the rhubarb is clearly the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, friendly British English with no restaurant jargon or health preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Yoghurt, fruit, nuts and seeds with only 2 tbsp honey make a balanced breakfast that a family would happily eat again.
